sn22.22:1.2: This discourse is much-quoted in later texts of both Pali and Sanskrit Buddhism, especially in discussions trying to resolve the question of what the Buddha meant by “person” (_puggala_). One school of Buddhism, the Pudgalavādins, argued that the “person” was as real as anything else, even if it could not be well defined, a position that was thouroughly rejected by other schools, including the Theravada ([kv1.1]()).
sn22.22:2.2: Note that the Jain meaning is “mass”, “matter”, while the sense “mass” is also found in Arthaśastra 2.14.7, 2.14.43 (of gold). The etymology is unclear, but it is a primarily Buddhist and Jain term, being absent from pre-Buddhist texts. The Jain _pudgala_ is an _astikāya_, connecting it with _sakkāya_.
sn22.22:3.2: As usual, I prefer to translate tatra tatra and related idioms as distributive.
